section.h2: Recent coding habits (computed from last 32 commits)

div.div: Commented on #81 Eventually move schema to nodeblocks

3 more thoughts:
We can / should define a schema for the descriptors themselves. We don't have to do this in one go, and I'd argue we shouldn't. We can deprecate the old style but keep it functional until we get everything updated one block at a time. We can use pre-commit to automate a full validation schema derived from these things and have autocomplete, error detection, inline documentation in VS Code
Commented on #2205 ✨ Add nodeblock descriptor yamls
Commented on #81 Eventually move schema to nodeblocks

Eventually, it would be nice to move the schema logic (with defaults and available options) to the nodeblock descriptors, instead of in one global place. I love the idea of decentralizing the schema, although I think we should have a central schema with controlled vocabularies and types that we can reuse. My leaning is to use JSON Schema (like @nx10 pitched in 2023), and we can have, a centralized schema that defines reusable subschemas that we use in these descriptors. For example, here, we could have something like { "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", (11 more lines were trimmed) in the schema and then something like Reorient BOLD: method: (5 more lines were trimmed) in the descriptor so then we just have to define a valid orientation once and we can use it anywhere in any of the nodeblocks. (and if we want YAML instead of JSON for the SSOT schema, we can do that like $schema: "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#" $id: "/CPAC/pipeline/schema.yaml" (16 more lines were trimmed) )
Commented on #82 Set up links to the nodeblock code/functions

I think we should just require
the descriptor is in a file with the same name (minus extension) as the nodeblock source code;
the descriptor file and the code file are siblings (in the same directory); and some requirement we define where
either the function name or the "name" in the Nodeblock decorator matches either the top-level key in the descriptor or that's what we fill in in the "source" field.
So for this example, we'd have @nodeblock( name="func_reorient", (6 more lines were trimmed) in CPAC/func_preproc/func_preproc.py and in CPAC/func_preproc/func_preproc.yaml we'd have func_reorient: description: (18 more lines were trimmed) or Reorient BOLD: description: (20 more lines were trimmed) then all we have to keep synced is the filenames and the nodeblock names, and the CI can match them up automatically.

div.div: Pytests: getting error function uses no argument error
singularity run error: No valid /bin/sh in container
For me this suggestion did the trick: when changing Singularity versions, configuration, or installation path, run make clean between make and make install in the installation process.
